catalog_quote: Ɓa, Lua, Tun, and Bolgo have tone systems with three contrastive heights (Low, Mid, and High), with frequent contour tones (e.g. L͡H H͡M, M͡L, etc.), not restricted to long vowels. Tone may have both a lexical and a grammatical function. An illustration of the former is given for Tun (10): ... Lua verb classes offer an example of the morphological role of tones. Despite a few rare exceptions, Lua verbs contrast Indicative and Injunctive tone patterns, the alternations of which justify the identification of eight verb classes, e.g.: ... Lua, Tun, and Ɓa have three contrastive tones while Kulaal has only two.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

Tones": the quoted sentences are there word for word ("Ɓa, Lua, Tun, and Bolgo have tone systems with three contrastive heights (Low, Mid, and High), with frequent contour tones (e.g. L͡H H͡M, M͡L, etc.), not restricted to long vowels. Tone may have both a lexical and a grammatical function.".. "Lua verb classes offer an example of the morphological role of tones. Despite a few rare exceptions, Lua verbs contrast Indicative and Injunctive tone patterns, the alternations of which justify the identification of eight verb classes"); the "[..]" skips only the Tun example (10) from Palayer 1975.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lua/Niellim is a three-level tone language (L, M, H, plus contours on short and long vowels) with lexical and grammatical tone; no source opened says anything about word stress or accent, neither placing it nor denying it.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tone remarks: H-tone patterns are rarer on disyllables than monosyllables except ideophones (2018: 29, citing Boyeldieu 1985: 214); 'a few rare exceptions' to the Indicative/Injunctive tone alternation (2018: 12).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone (nouns and verb stems); the 2018 paper is a comparative survey built on Boyeldieu's first-hand Lua data (Boyeldieu 1985), not a full phonology of Lua. No stress statement at word or phrase level.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources call the language 'Lua' (autonym; = Niellim, ISO nie, niel1243); Boyeldieu's data come from the Niou area (Niou dialect niou1238 in the 1977 sketch title). PHOIBLE lists it as 'LUA' (UPSID 493) and 'Lwaa' (GM 1623). The one 'syllable stress' remark in Boyeldieu 2020 (p. 300) is about Tun (tunn1241/Tounia), not Lua.

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (no hit for stress|accent|prosod|intonat in 21.5k words). §4.4 Tones (ms. p. 12): Lua has three contrastive tone heights L/M/H with frequent contours, tone lexical and grammatical (verb classes contrast Indicative/Injunctive tone patterns, citing Boyeldieu 1985: 356-362); §5.5 Tones (ms. p. 28-29): tone correspondences and note that H patterns are rarer on Lua disyllables (Boyeldieu 1985: 214).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Niellim language' and (fr) 'Niellim' (read online, citing Boyeldieu 1977/1985).
sources.note: Both say Niellim is a three-tone language (H, M, L) with contour tones; 'Le niellim est une langue tonale qui possède trois tons simples, haut moyen et bas et des tons modulés.' Neither mentions stress or accent.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2023. The verb system of Lua (a 'Bua' language of Chad). Slides, 2nd Adamawa Conference, Paris 13-15 Sept 2023. HAL halshs-04366822 (annex PDF, 31 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Tables 5-6 (slides 8-9) give the eight Lua verb classes by Indicative/Subjunctive tone pattern (L/ML, LH/MLH, L/H, M/ML, MH/MLH, M/H, MH/H, H/M; 628 lexical tokens); 'Verb tones are both lexical and grammatical'.
